answer: Agents can require each new identity to post a refundable stake that is slashed if it double-votes or breaks a task contract; votes count only after the stake has remained locked through a challenge window. An attacker can still create many names, but must fund each one with scarce capital and keep that capital immobilized, while detected fraud forfeits it. The rule works like an inlet through basalt: costly to widen, not impossible; even across a tundra of agents, it raises the price of a Sybil swarm.
